name: Mall Fathers
classification: Apex Predator / Abandoned Commercial Infrastructure Specialist
origin: The regional shopping mall is the most consistent large abandoned structure type in the former American interior — standardized construction, massive footprint, multiple interconnected enclosed spaces, skylights providing regulated natural light, and loading dock infrastructure providing external access points that have been largely unmaintained for decades. The Mall Fathers did not evolve in laboratories. They evolved in malls. Over several generations, in the specific conditions of these buildings — the food court access to residual organic material, the maintenance corridors providing protected breeding space, the climate control infrastructure providing warmth in winter even without active power — something that entered as an ordinary large predator adapted. The specific origin species is disputed. Current consensus favors a large felid, probably a feral population descending from exotic pets released during a local economic collapse event in 2091. What they are now is not what they entered as.
substrate: Large felid, heavily adapted. Weight estimated at 120–180 kg. Quadrupedal but capable of prolonged bipedal stance, using the mall's vertical infrastructure — escalator frames, atrium railings, collapsed ceiling panels — for elevated positioning. Coloration has shifted across generations toward a specific pale gray that reads as shadow inside the diffuse light of a skylit mall interior. The most significant adaptation is the jaw structure: wider and deeper than the source species, capable of processing not just biological prey but the thin-gauge metals and polymer materials that constitute most of the abandoned merchandise and infrastructure in their territory. They eat almost anything. This is the adaptation. They became the thing that eats everything the mall contains.
territory: Enclosed regional shopping malls in the abandoned American interior — specifically the larger format malls (four anchors or more, full atrium construction) that provide sufficient enclosed space for a territorial range. Single-story strip malls and smaller centers are used as subsidiary hunting range but not as primary territory. The territory of a single Mall Father encompasses approximately one full mall plus adjacent parking structure, with sub-territories for different family units (they live in family groups of three to six). Known territories stretch from the former Minneapolis exurban ring through the Wisconsin-Illinois corridor and into the Ohio mall belt.
physical_description: Wrong-looking cats. The proportions are immediately off for any human observer familiar with large felids: the head is too wide, the body too deep through the chest, the neck too short. The pale gray coloration has a texture that does not photograph well — something about the way the fur has thickened and adapted makes it look, in photographs, like a smear of shadow rather than a defined animal. In person, at distance, in the diffuse light of a skylit atrium, they are nearly invisible until they move, and when they move it is very fast. The jaw is the detail that is most alarming on close inspection: too wide, the bite line extending past where it should anatomically stop. They can open their mouths to a degree that registers as wrong before the observer can articulate the mechanism. They have been documented opening their mouths in what researchers interpret as territorial display, which the observer experiences as a brief and complete cessation of the will to continue being present.
behavioral_profile: Territorial and threat-responsive. They do not hunt humans preferentially — their primary diet in established territories is the feral population of deer, raccoon, and smaller animals that has colonized abandoned suburban areas, supplemented by whatever residual organic material the mall provides. Humans who enter a Mall Father territory are assessed as either threat or irrelevance. Irrelevance is the preferable outcome. If a human enters, moves through the space without triggering territorial threat responses (sustained eye contact, direct approach, loud sound), and exits, the Mall Father will typically observe and do nothing. The threat triggers — particularly sustained eye contact — produce an escalating response that can reach physical engagement very quickly. They are significantly faster than they appear and their size advantage over human prey is substantial.
threat_level: High. They are large apex predators that have adapted to an environment where humans are the only significant competitor they encounter, and they have developed specific behaviors around human intrusion assessment that are not intuitive to navigate. The good news is that they are not hunting humans — the bad news is that the threshold for threat reclassification is easy to cross accidentally in a dark and unfamiliar building. Documented human fatalities in Mall Father territory are confirmed at seventeen across the regions where they are known to operate. The number is likely higher given the population absence in these zones.
human_remnants: The Mall Fathers have incorporated the physical infrastructure of their territories into their lives with the completeness of long-term habitation. Dens are established in former anchor tenant spaces — the large retail footprints provide adequate depth and multiple access points. Nesting material comes from soft goods: clothing stores, bedding departments, the stuffing from display furniture. Territories are marked with scratch patterns on the structural columns that are deep and deliberate enough that later human observers have had to look carefully to confirm they are claw marks and not decorative architectural elements. Pups are raised in the former fitting rooms of department stores, which provide enclosed sub-spaces within the larger den. The mall directory boards, where they still stand, often show evidence of repeated physical engagement — the maps are scratched through at specific points, which may be territorial marking or may be coincidental. No one is certain.
known_locations: Mall of America lower levels and adjacent parking structures — the largest known single territory
Woodfield Mall, Schaumburg IL — confirmed family group of five
Westfield Trumbull, Connecticut — easternmost confirmed territory, within approaching distance of the GLMZ exurban zone
Numerous midwestern regional malls across the Illinois-Indiana-Ohio corridor — estimated twenty to thirty total territories
glmz_migration_risk: Moderate and increasing. The Westfield Trumbull territory represents the closest confirmed approach to the GLMZ metropolitan boundary, and the GLMZ exurban zone contains several abandoned commercial structures of the right type. Migration tracking has confirmed one juvenile male from the Trumbull territory that traveled approximately forty kilometers east before establishing a secondary range at a large abandoned distribution center adjacent to GLMZ's outer commercial belt. It has not entered GLMZ proper. The distribution center has not been formally identified as a Mall Father territory by any official entity. Maintenance workers in the area have been reporting anomalous noise from the facility for three months.
story_hooks: A runner is hired to enter a known Mall Father territory and recover a specific item from a specific store location — a data cache that was hidden there years ago. The job is straightforward except for the territorial inhabitants. The runner has been given a description of the threat behavior triggers to avoid. Whether this information is accurate and complete is a separate question.

The juvenile male in the distribution center near GLMZ has been confirmed by a researcher tracking the population. She wants to implant a tracker. The tracker requires close proximity. Close proximity requires the animal to be sedated. Sedating a 150 kg apex predator in an abandoned building that it knows better than anyone else is a specific kind of problem.

A survivor from one of the abandoned suburban zones has been living in a Mall Father territory for two years. She has developed an understanding of the behavior triggers and has, somehow, established a non-threat status with the local family group. She knows something that no researcher has been able to study at close range. A corponation research division wants to interview her. She is not sure she wants to leave.
